APPROACH TO ATRIAL FIBRILLATION 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
UNSTABLE AF causing: 
 
*Hypotension 
*Acute cardiac failure 
*Chest pain 
*Dyspnoea 
*Altered mental status 
Is the patient STABLE?  
MANAGEMENT 
1.Cardioversion 
 
-150-200J 
 
-consider using max dose first 
 
-max 3 attempts 
 
-BP preserving analgesia/sedation   
              (fentanyl;ketamine/dormicum) 
2. Anti-coagulation 
-Balance between risk (HAS-BLED) &      
  benefit (CHA2DS2VASc) 
-start Clexane 1mg/kg SC stat in ED if       
  no contraindications 
CARDIOVERSION FAILS 
 
Rate control 
- First exclude WPW (**see ECG and box below**)  
à NO CONTROL AGENTS 
-Amiodarone 150mg IVI in D5W over 30min then  
         900mg in 200ml D5W @ 8.3mls/hr 
-Consider MgSO4 2-4g IVI over 15min 
Dr K Jacobs / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
RATE CONTROL 
(GOAL < 110bpm) 
MANAGEMENT 
*Synchronised cardioversion 
*Analgesia & sedation 
*Consider anticoagulation 
        -Balance between risk (HAS-BLED)  
         & benefit (CHA2DS2VASc) 
        -start Clexane 1mg/kg SC stat in ED if     
         no contraindications 
CANDIDATE FOR CARDIOVERSION? 
 
*< 48hrs 
*New onset 
*No LV dysfunction 
*No valvular heart disease 
*No history of VTE 
*Therapeutic anticoagulation 
NO

*Amiodarone 
        
150mg IVI in D5W over 30min then 
         
900mg in 200ml D5W @ 8.3mls/hr 
*Beta-blocker 
 
-Carvedilol 3.125mg stat po or 
 
-Atenolol 50mg stat po or 
 
-Propranolol if thyroid associated 
*Calcium channel blocker 
*Digoxin 
Look for and treat underlying cause 
“The Atrial Fibs” 
 
T: Thyroid Dx 
H: Hypothermia 
E: Embolism (PE) 
 
 
 
A: Alcohol 
T: Trauma (cardiac contusion) 
R: Recent surgery (e.g. CABG) 
I: Ischaemia 
A: Atrial enlargement 
L: Lone/idiopathic 
F: Fever/anaemia/high out-put states 
I: Infarct 
B: Bad valves (e.g. Mitral stenosis) 
S: Stimulants (Cocaine, theophylline, caffeine)

Dr K Jacobs / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
Recent evidence: No survival benefit in rate vs rhythm control  
Rate control and anticoagulation supported by recent trials
